stories.title: Law Firm Nutter Expands to 11K SF at Durst’s 5 Grand Central East
stories.excerpt: Law firm Nutter is taking more office space at one of the Durst Organization’s buildings near Grand Central Terminal, Commercial Observer has learned. Nutter, which is based in Boston and provides personal and business legal services, has signed a deal to renew its existing 5,719 square feet on the 27th floor of Durst’s 5 Grand Central East — also known as 655 Third Avenue — and add another 5,719 square feet on the entire 25th floor, according to the landlord. The deal brings the law firm’s total footprint at the 30-story office tower to 11,438 square feet. “The Manhattan office leasing market is surging, especially for Class A spaces in transit-accessible locations such as Grand Central East,” Jody Durst, president of Durst, said in a statement. “Nutter’s decision to expand at 5 Grand Central East reflects the desirability of the area and Durst’s long-term investment in our buildings.” The length of the lease was not provided, but the asking rent was $80 per square foot, according to Durst. CBRE’s Michael Joyce and Trevor Larkin brokered the deal for Nutter, while Durst was repped in-house by Tom Bow, Ashlea Aaron, Bailey Caliban and Sayo Kamara. A spokesperson for CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Nutter, which was founded in 1879, has been a tenant in Durst’s office building between East 41st and East 42nd streets since 2022. Michael Scott, co-managing partner of Nutter, said in a statement that 5 Grand Central East is “the right location for our clients and our team as we grow.” In December, Durst rebranded two of its office buildings near Grand Central, turning 655 Third Avenue to 5 Grand Central East and renaming 733 Third Avenue as 11 Grand Central East. The rebranding reflected its “continued investment in the Grand Central submarket,” the firm said. bullets: Nutter law firm expands 11.4K SF at Durst's 5 Grand Central East, Manhattan.
Class A Midtown office asking rent $80/SF; landlord cites transit-access desirability.
Manhattan office leasing market described as 'surging' by major landlord.
stories.summary: Boston-based law firm Nutter renewed and doubled its footprint at Durst's 5 Grand Central East (655 Third Avenue) to 11,438 SF total, with the expansion taking an entire 25th floor at $80/SF asking rent. Durst highlighted strong demand for Class A space near Grand Central Terminal. The deal signals continued institutional confidence in Midtown's transit-anchored office stock.
stories.impact: Office leasing strength in transit-rich Midtown Manhattan does not directly compete for multifamily capital but signals robust white-collar employment and professional services demand in Manhattan. This supports underlying multifamily fundamentals—high-income renter base with stable job anchors—and validates continued investment in Midtown residential adjacent to job centers like Grand Central East.

stories.title: Koeppel Rosen Arranges Three Office Leases in Midtown, Midtown South
stories.excerpt: Koeppel Rosen LLC, leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, has arranged nearly 18,000 square feet of new office space leases, comprised of separate transactions at three different properties in the company’s portfolio.  Max Koeppel represented Koeppel Rosen in-house on all three leases. The transactions include the following: MNRK Music Group L.P., an independent music company, has agreed to a 7,629-square-foot lease at 443 Park Ave. South. The lease includes a seven-year, seven-month termt. Luke Dillmeier, Patrick Heeg, and Thomas Hines with Transwestern represented the tenant. AL Diamond Home Products LLC, an importer and distributor of household goods, has agreed to a 7,272-square-foot lease at 20 W. 36th St. The lease includes a seven-year, seven-month term. Joel Kubie with Benchmark represented the tenant. Kevin V. Lehman DDS, a New York City dental practice, has agreed to a 3,096-square-foot lease at 154 W. 14th St. The lease includes a 12-year, 10-month term. Todd Hershmann and Josh Gosin with Newmark represented the tenant. The post Koeppel Rosen Arranges Three Office Leases in Midtown, Midtown South appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Koeppel Rosen arranges 18K SF office leases across three Midtown/Midtown South properties.
Transaction details and specific rents not disclosed in press release.
Portfolio activity reflects continued leasing activity in core Manhattan office submarkets.
stories.summary: Koeppel Rosen announced three separate office leases totaling nearly 18,000 SF in Midtown and Midtown South, with Max Koeppel representing the Rosen family portfolio in-house on all transactions. Specific lease terms, rents, and tenant names were not provided.
stories.impact: Minimal direct signal. Aggregate office leasing activity in Midtown suggests steady occupancy but lack of disclosed terms, rents, or submarkets prevents assessment of market momentum or tenant quality shifts that would inform adjacent multifamily demand.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 490-Unit Multifamily in St. Louis
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced the sale of Trinity Park Apartments, a 490-unit multifamily property in North St. Louis. The property was sold through an online live bid auction sale conducted by Marcus & Millichap. “Trinity Park Apartments offered investors a significant value-add opportunity,” said Ryan D. Engle, senior managing director investments. “The property’s below-market occupancy presented a substantial lease-up opportunity for the new ownership.” Engle, Andrean Angelov and Aaron Kuroiwa, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Chicago Oak Brook and Indianapolis offices, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller. Engle and Angelov, along with Mike Cusick in the firm’s St. Louis office, procured the buyer. The agents collaborated with Adam Sklaver and Philip Kates of Marcus & Millichap’s auction services to market the asset and assist in securing the buyer. Trinity Park Apartments, located at 11065 Dunklin Drive, spans 24.08 acres and consists of 34 residential buildings including 285 one-bedroom and 205 two-bedroom residences. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 490-Unit Multifamily in St. Louis appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trinity Park Apartments, 490 units, North St. Louis sold via Marcus & Millichap auction.
Property had below-market occupancy; described as value-add lease-up opportunity.
24-acre site on Dunklin Drive: 285 one-bed, 205 two-bed units across 34 buildings.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale of Trinity Park Apartments, a 490-unit property in North St. Louis, via online live auction. The property was marketed as a significant value-add opportunity with below-market occupancy, indicating the new owner has a lease-up mandate. The site spans 24 acres with mixed one- and two-bedroom floor plans.
stories.impact: Below-market occupancy at a 490-unit asset in North St. Louis suggests North County St. Louis multifamily market faces absorption headwinds or supply oversupply. New ownership's value-add focus implies rent growth opportunity, but the initial distress signals competitive supply pressure in the submarket. For developers, this reflects a buyer's market for repositioning, not new supply momentum.

stories.title: Hanover Company Launches Construction on Its First SoCal Industrial
stories.excerpt: Hanover Company, alongside its capital partner, a real estate fund advised by Crow Holdings Capital, has begun construction on a ground-up industrial development in Simi Valley. The project marks the developer’s debut in the region. The approximately 200,000-square-foot building sits on a 13-acre site at 903 Quimisa Dr. With immediate proximity to CA 118, the project will feature 36’ clear heights, an 8.5” slab, skylights and ample employee parking. “We are thrilled to bring Hanover Industrial’s first project to Southern California and to establish a presence in the dynamic Simi Valley market,” said Anthony Feenick, development partner at Hanover Company. “We are grateful for our continued partnership with the team at Crow Holdings Capital on this endeavor and look forward to seeing the project come to fruition.” Located off the 118 freeway, the project is designed to accommodate a variety of users, including corporate headquarters, packaging and assembly or distribution. The post Hanover Company Launches Construction on Its First SoCal Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hanover Company breaks ground, 200K SF industrial in Simi Valley with Crow Holdings Capital.
First Southern California industrial project; 13-acre site, 36' clear heights, CA-118 access.
Target users: corporate HQ, packaging, assembly, distribution; strong logistics corridor positioning.
stories.summary: Hanover Company and Crow Holdings Capital have begun construction on a 200,000 SF ground-up industrial development in Simi Valley, CA (903 Quimisa Dr.), marking Hanover's regional debut. The project sits on 13 acres with 36' clear heights, an 8.5" slab, and immediate CA-118 freeway access, designed to serve corporate, packaging, assembly, and distribution users.
stories.impact: Hanover's entry into Simi Valley industrial with Crow Holdings Capital partnership signals confidence in Southern California logistics and manufacturing tenant demand. While not multifamily, this reflects capital reallocation and regional growth expectations in SoCal; robust industrial absorption can indicate labor in-migration and wage growth that supports downstream multifamily rental demand across greater Los Angeles metro. Monitor Simi Valley and surrounding submarkets for renter population inflows.

stories.title: Associated Bank Finalizes Loan for Twelve-Acre Retail Project in OH
stories.excerpt: Associated Bank announced the completion of a $9 million loan to GTZ Properties for development of Trailhead Crossing, a multi-building retail project at 1135-1131 US-36 in Delaware, Ohio, a suburb of Columbus. The twelve-acre project will consist of three freestanding buildings occupied by Chik-Fil-A, Chipotle Mexican Grill and Take 5 Oil Change; a second three-tenant strip will be occupied by Dunkin Donuts, Nothing Bundt Cakes and Pacific Dental Services. Of two pad-ready sites, one is already pending sale to a national daycare company. A later phase of the development will be anchored by a big-box national retailer. GTZ Properties is a Highland Park, Illinois, based full-service commercial real estate development and investment company specializing in retail-related properties nationwide that is headed by Mitch Goltz and Jeremy Forman. Daniel Barrins, a senior vice president with Associated Bank’s Commercial Real Estate division in Chicago, managed the loan arrangements and closing. This is Associated Bank’s 18th loan to GTZ Properties principal Mitch Goltz. The post Associated Bank Finalizes Loan for Twelve-Acre Retail Project in OH appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Associated Bank funds $9M loan for Trailhead Crossing retail, Delaware, Ohio (Columbus suburb).
Multi-building development: Chick-fil-A, Chipotle, Take 5; Dunkin, Nothng Bundt Cakes, Pacific Dental.
One pad-ready site pending daycare company sale; later phase anchored by big-box retailer.
stories.summary: Associated Bank closed a $9 million construction loan for GTZ Properties' Trailhead Crossing, a 12-acre retail project in Delaware, Ohio (Columbus suburb) comprising freestanding buildings and a multi-tenant strip with major QSR and service tenants. One pad-ready parcel is pending sale to a national daycare operator, with a later phase anchored by a big-box national retailer. This is Associated Bank's 18th deal with GTZ Properties principal Mitch Goltz.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily. Retail development activity in Delaware, Ohio (US-36 corridor) signals local commercial growth and service-sector investment in a Columbus suburb, which may support underlying demographic stability and consumer income in the area, but does not directly inform apartment supply, demand, or capital dynamics.

stories.title: Planet Fitness to Open at Sky Three Residences in West Brighton Beach
stories.excerpt: Planet Fitness has signed a lease for 14,520 square feet of retail space at the base of Tower 3 at Sky Three Residences, 532 Neptune Ave. in Brooklyn’s West Brighton Beach neighborhood. Located along the Neptune Avenue corridor, the new gym will complement the neighborhood’s growing mix of retail uses and is expected to open in early 2027. CBRE represented Planet Fitness in the transaction, while Commercial Acquisitions represented the landlord. Planet Fitness will join Sky Three’s growing ground-floor retail lineup, which includes CVS Pharmacy, NetCost Market, Starbucks, Flower Heaven NYC, Sky Mocha and Kings Barbershop. Flower Heaven offers Sky Three residents an exclusive 10% discount, while Sky Mocha provides delivery throughout the property’s amenity spaces, including directly to its resort-style pool. The post Planet Fitness to Open at Sky Three Residences in West Brighton Beach appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Planet Fitness signs 14.5K SF ground-floor lease at Sky Three Residences, Brooklyn.
Tower 3 base; Neptune Avenue corridor, West Brighton Beach; opening early 2027.
Retail mix includes CVS, NetCost, Starbucks, specialty dining; builds community amenity ecosystem.
stories.summary: Planet Fitness has leased 14,520 SF of ground-floor retail space at Tower 3 of Sky Three Residences (532 Neptune Ave., Brooklyn's West Brighton Beach) with an expected opening in early 2027. The gym will join an existing retail lineup including CVS, NetCost Market, Starbucks, and specialty dining and beverage concepts, many offering resident incentives.
stories.impact: Sky Three Residences is a multifamily-anchored mixed-use development; Planet Fitness addition strengthens ground-floor activation and resident amenity value, improving leasing velocity and retention. The presence of an anchor fitness brand, combined with food and pharmacy tenants, increases competitive appeal against other West Brighton Beach and Coney Island/Brooklyn waterfront rental properties. This benefits operator economics but does not alter neighborhood supply or demand fundamentals—it optimizes existing asset performance.

stories.title: Sheppard Takes 107K SF at In-Rel’s D.C. Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: One of the 50 highest-grossing law firms in the U.S. has signed an anchor lease at a planned Washington, D.C., trophy office redevelopment three years before its anticipated completion. Law firm Sheppard signed for 107,224 square feet at In-Rel Properties’ 2033 K Street NW, CBRE announced Tuesday. The firm, which has more than 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices, will move in after the building’s expected completion in July 2029. The brokerage did not disclose the value of the lease or the asking rent. In-Rel is expanding and updating the existing building, located along K Street near the intersection of D.C.’s Central Business District, West End and Dupont Circle. The developer will retain the property’s concrete structure while expanding it vertically and horizontally, including adding three floors and a penthouse. The renovations are another example of owners betting on Washington’s bifurcated office market, where distress coexists with a shortage of large, new trophy spaces, particularly for law firms and other high-end tenants. “We all know D.C. has plenty of office space, but what it doesn’t have is enough large-block, trophy-quality product that leading law firms like Sheppard demand,” In-Rel CEO Jackson Siegal said in a statement. Sheppard Chair Luca Salvi said the new office would provide a more modern and efficient workplace as the firm approaches its centennial and continues growing its Washington operation. CBRE’s Dimitri Hajimihalis, Emily Eppolito and Carroll Cavanagh represented In-Rel. Savills’ Gary Stein, David Lipson, Jon Glass and Owen Jaccard represented Sheppard. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Sheppard law firm signs 107.2K SF anchor lease at In-Rel's 2033 K Street NW, D.C.
Building completion July 2029; firm occupies major trophy office pre-completion three years out.
In-Rel expanding/renovating: adding 3 floors + penthouse; K Street near West End/Dupont Circle.
stories.summary: Sheppard, a top-50 U.S. law firm (1,200+ attorneys, 16 offices), signed an anchor lease for 107,224 SF at In-Rel Properties' planned redevelopment of 2033 K Street NW in Washington, D.C., with occupancy planned for July 2029. The developer is expanding and renovating the existing structure by adding three floors and a penthouse. The lease underscores developer confidence in demand for new trophy office in D.C.'s central business district.
stories.impact: Major law firm anchor lease three years pre-completion signals strong D.C. office market bifurcation—distressed obsolete stock alongside shortage of large, modern trophy spaces. This validates In-Rel's capital commitment and de-risks the redevelopment. For multifamily: sustained demand for prime downtown office space reinforces professional-services employment concentration and high-income renter base in D.C. central markets (West End, Dupont Circle), supporting premium apartment demand in adjacent neighborhoods and future residential development upside along K Street corridor.

stories.title: Eliot Spitzer Gains State Approval to Redevelop 985 Fifth Avenue After Legal Bout
stories.excerpt: Former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer will finally get to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue after suing the state to obtain approval. Spitzer claimed that the state’s Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) was delaying the approval of an application to not renew rent-stabilized leases in the building, a necessary step before the property could be redeveloped. Spitzer ultimately won the state’s blessing. The two-year request to end the rent-stabilized leases on the property followed approval from the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 2023 to take a wrecking ball to the 25-story rental property and construct luxury condominiums in its place. Spitzer alleged potential misconduct in the lawsuit, reported by The Real Deal. Spitzer could not be reached for comment. HCR, now under the administration of Gov. Kathy Hochul, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Spitzer’s Spitzer Enterprises has been advancing on other aspects of the project despite the delay, unveiling designs by SLCE Architects for the property in November 2025 which would yield 25 condo units, according to New York YIMBY. The former governor, who resigned in 2008 during a prostitution scandal, has owned the property since at least 2018 after buying seven residential buildings in the city, including 800 Fifth Avenue, with a total of 1.5 million square feet. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Eliot Spitzer wins state court approval to deconvert 985 Fifth Avenue rent-stabilized building.
NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission approved demolition in 2023; HCR lease non-renewal delayed 2 years.
Plans: demolish 25-story rental, build luxury condos; SLCE Architects designs released November 2024.
stories.summary: Former Gov. Eliot Spitzer obtained state approval to end rent-stabilized leases at 985 Fifth Avenue and proceed with demolition, following a lawsuit against the state's Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) over delayed approval. The NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission had already approved demolition in 2023. Spitzer plans to demolish the 25-story building and replace it with luxury condominiums designed by SLCE Architects.
stories.impact: This high-profile Fifth Avenue conversion removes a multifamily rental asset from Manhattan's stock and converts it to for-sale condominiums, reducing rental supply in one of Manhattan's most exclusive neighborhoods. While the departure of rent-stabilized units may reduce regulatory friction, the net effect is a loss of 985 Fifth Avenue as a rental product. The precedent of successful deconversion after regulatory battle (and Landmarks approval already in hand) may embolden other condo conversions in prime Manhattan locations, tightening rental supply and supporting elevated rents in competing premium multifamily assets nearby (Upper East Side, Central Park South adjacent). Monitor for follow-on conversions.

stories.title: OCVibe Adds Five Dining Concepts to $5B SoCal District
stories.excerpt: The Samueli family has added five more dining concepts to the 50,000-square-foot market hall set to open next year as part of the $5 billion mixed-use development called OCVibe surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, Calif. Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll and Gelato Paradiso are the five new food options, adding Mexican, Filipino, Northern Chinese and Italian menus to the 21-kitchen market hall named Katella Commons. They join a growing roster at OCVibe, which earlier added concepts from chefs behind Amiga Amore, Burritos La Palma, Evil Cooks, Manaao Thai Comfort Food and Darkroom Restaurant and Wine Bar. Beloved Los Angeles chef Roy Choi is also bringing his Best Friend restaurant to the district. OCVibe did not disclose the values of the leases or the sizes of each space. Sources familiar with the development told Commercial Observer that OCVibe is fronting the initial investment, which averages around $300,000 per stall, as well as providing ongoing operational supports. “We wanted to approach this differently than a traditional landlord-tenant relationship,” OCVibe Senior Vice President Scott Frick said in a statement shared with CO. “Independent chefs are often asked to take on significant financial and operational risk before they ever serve their first meal. And unfortunately, many restaurants fail because of the significant upfront investment required of them.” Indeed, Frick recently told Commercial Observer that the Samueli family’s ownership structure has allowed the project to take a hands-on approach to restaurant leasing. Ownership is funding Katella Commons down to the kitchen equipment, allowing tenants to avoid substantial upfront costs of fitting out the new spaces. “Any tenant that comes in doesn’t have to come in with capital to fit out the kitchen — basically bring in your own knives and we’ll turn on the menu boards,” Frick said. bullets: OCVibe adds five dining concepts to $5B Samueli mixed-use district, Anaheim, near Honda Center.
50K SF Katella Commons market hall opening 2025; 21 kitchens total; OCVibe fronting ~$300K per stall.
Concepts: Don Churros Gomez, MFK, Mojo, Pull & Roll, Gelato Paradiso; Roy Choi's Best Friend added.
stories.summary: The Samueli family's OCVibe development in Anaheim announced five additional dining concepts for the 50,000 SF Katella Commons market hall opening in 2025, bringing total kitchens to 21. Tenants include Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll, and Gelato Paradiso, complementing earlier leases with Roy Choi's Best Friend restaurant and other chefs. OCVibe is funding approximately $300K initial investment per stall plus ongoing operational support.
stories.impact: OCVibe is a $5B mixed-use district anchored by Honda Center (sports/entertainment); robust food-hall and dining activation signals strong regional draw and foot traffic, which supports multifamily renter base retention and attraction. Heavy developer subsidy of food-hall tenants ($300K per stall) indicates below-market initial economics but a bet on long-term district density and captive renter/visitor population. For multifamily developers in Anaheim and greater Orange County, OCVibe's maturation as a live-work-play destination increases competitive pressure to build adjacent or integrated residential, signaling future apartment supply opportunities in the Honda Center trade area.

stories.title: The New School Sells Loeb Hall Residence to Hawkins Way Capital for $52M
stories.excerpt: In its third acquisition of student housing in Manhattan this summer, Hawkins Way Capital has purchased a residence hall near Union Square for $51.5 million from the New School, according to city records made public Tuesday. Hawkins, using the entity 135 E 12th Owner, bought Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, directly from The New School, records show. Joshua Bird, managing director and general counsel at Hawkins, signed the deal for the buyer, while Loretta Ferrari, chief financial officer at the New School, signed for the seller. “We’ve long been looking for the right opportunity in this neighborhood, and this property represents an ideal addition to our portfolio,” Ross Walker, managing partner at Hawkins, said in a statement to Commercial Observer. “Its location, existing student housing infrastructure and flexibility put us in an ideal position to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country’s strongest urban student housing markets.” It’s unclear why the New School stopped using Loeb Hall as an active dormitory for its students, but the property was removed from its undergraduate housing options this year. Loeb Hall is four blocks east of the New School’s main University Center and administrative offices on Fifth Avenue, although the sprawling urban campus has numerous sites near Union Square. The former Loeb Hall will undergo renovations and be repositioned under Hawkins’ Found Study student housing platform, according to a spokesperson for Hawkins. It’s unclear who brokered the recent sale. A spokesperson for the New School did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal is Hawkins’ third major student housing acquisition in Manhattan in recent months. bullets: Hawkins Way Capital purchases Loeb Hall, 268-bed student housing, Union Square for $51.5M.
The New School direct sale; Hawkins' third Manhattan student housing acquisition this summer.
131–135 East 12th Street; described as strong urban student housing market with flex potential.
stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital acquired Loeb Hall, a 268-bed student residence hall at 131–135 East 12th Street near Union Square, from The New School for $51.5 million. This marks Hawkins Way's third Manhattan student housing purchase in summer 2024. The buyer cited the property's location, existing dormitory infrastructure, and operational flexibility as drivers of the acquisition in what it described as one of the country's strongest urban student housing markets.
stories.impact: Repeat institutional buying of Manhattan student housing (three acquisitions in one summer) signals strong capital conviction and pricing discipline in the sector. The New School's sale of Loeb Hall suggests universities are increasingly willing to monetize student housing assets rather than operate in-house, opening the market to professional operators. For multifamily developers, this reflects capital competing in the student housing niche; however, student housing and traditional multifamily are distinct products. Monitor NYC's student housing market for operator professionalization and for potential downstream conversion to conventional rental if student enrollment softens—a tail risk that could flood supply into the broader Manhattan rental market.
